items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: The interviewee mentions Clarence Williams only in the context of Pops Foster's interview, stating that Pops mentioned they had to get people like Clarence Williams to write down tunes for Jelly Roll Morton. The interviewee does not describe a personal relationship with Clarence Williams.

ctx.x: That he improvises better or something like that. I don't...

You'd have a hard time making that argument stick, though, too, with a person like Louis, who learned to read very well, I guess, in the 20s on the boat, and then even took lessons in Chicago. And, of course, Bunk always could probably read quite well ever since he started. In fact, that's the way Bunk advised us starting in music. First in the solfège, as they call it, the old European classical sight reading and ear training, where you have to learn to sing the melodies just by looking at them without playing…
No. Was Buddy Bolden a reader? Did anyone know?

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Chester's artist is very good. He usually gets a real arousing...

ctx.x: Sound like Chester's Arbs on this.
Chester's artist is very good. He usually gets a real arousing...
Usually Chink, you know, looks like he's half asleep over there leaning against the wall.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: I'll go over the notes from people such as Clarence Williams. I have about four pages on Clarence Williams... I'll get something about Clarence Williams, which was done in New York.

ctx.x: The early ones are not available?

No, at best. And also, I have a note here I noticed right here in front of me. I think the 1919 and 1920 files were missing, even in 1938 when I went there, in December of 1938. But I have some of these notes, which I'll go over, and might be able to enlarge a little bit on them. These are rather sketchy. Put on ahead. I mean, I'll send them down to Missouri. I see. Because it's a job that's going to take hours and days to go over that. And I'll copy it out, and it'll have to be by longhand, and I'll send a…
There's also a lot of material there that's invaluable. And we ought to be sure and get recorded some way.
